decisions.evidence: Band1, line 1, after יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ: there is a clear word space between עַל and כָּל, with no raised stroke. The maqaf after כָּל is clearly printed. The full page agrees.

Band1, line 2: מַה־שֶּׁבָּרָאתָ runs straight into וְיִירָאוּךָ with only a word space. There is no period dot on the baseline. The paragraph's only stop is the sof-pasuq colon after the second שֶּׁבָּרָאתָ at the end of line 5.
Band1, line 3, after אֲגֻדָּה: the marks under both א and ח are short flat bars with no lower tick, so both are patah. There is no segol triangle under א, and the mark under ח has no qamats stem.

Band2, Vetimlokh line 1: there is an open word space between בְּהַר and צִיּוֹן with no top-line stroke. Compare the visible maqaf in כָּל־מַעֲשֶׂיךָ on the same line.

Band2, Vetimlokh line 3, Ps 146:10 (not the MiKhamokha116 Name sent to the human). The sheva under י and the qamats under ו are clear. A small dark speck may sit high near the ה/ו junction, but at band resolution I can't tell whether it is a holam or what it sits on (ה versus ו). The first reader also flagged it as uncertain between יְהֹוָה and יְהוָֹה. Neither reading is confirmed. This needs a higher-resolution crop or the human.
Band2, Kadosh line 1: there is a period after מִבַּלְעָדֶיךָ. Then כַּכָּתוּב ends the line at the margin with no dot. Line 2 starts with וַיִּגְבַּהּ.

Band2, Kadosh line 2, after וְהָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ: the vowel under ד is a short flat bar with no descending stem, so it is patah. Qamats in this font is a visible T shape, as in the qamats of הַקָּדוֹשׁ just before it. The dagesh in ד is visible. The full page agrees.
